editorial.headline: Five-Star Hotels: Open Nationally, Conditional in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers short-stay five-star hotel accommodation, from furnished suites to direct on-site guest service, across small, medium and large business scales.
editorial.body:
Five-star hotel activity is, at its core, the provision of short-stay accommodation on a daily or weekly basis. It applies to establishments that meet five-star hotel requirements and use part or all of a building, whether the building area is at or below 6,000 square metres or above it. The description is not limited to a room key and a reception desk: it contemplates furnished living areas and suites, with the direct, on-site customer service that defines a full hotel operation.

The operational picture can be correspondingly broad. Daily cleaning and bed-making, food and beverage service, laundry, and conference or convention facilities may all sit within the activity. These are not separate promises or regulatory conditions; they are the additional services expressly contemplated within the stated hotel accommodation scope. The activity is open to businesses at small, medium and large scales, giving the classification room to describe both compact five-star properties and larger hotel operations.

Nationally, the activity is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Bali requires a more exact reading. Its status is conditional on scope rather than categorically blocked: some scope(s) assessed through OSS at the large-business scale are low risk, while others carry a higher risk assessment. Bali’s permanent, island-wide rule blocks all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities from PMA registration. For this hotel activity, PMA registration in Bali is therefore possible only where the declared activity falls under the higher-risk scope; the exact activity must be checked live in OSS.

That distinction matters because a national opening does not, by itself, settle the Bali registration outcome. The national position remains fully open to foreign ownership, while the Bali result turns on the risk classification attached to the precise scope declared in OSS. For an investor or operator, the practical task is to align the proposed hotel activity with its actual scope before treating Bali registration as available.
